I have all the context I need. Let me now answer as the farmer.

---

I am 68 years old, and I have been farming in Quzhou County my whole life. I only finished primary school, so I do not know all the fancy words from the agricultural station, but I know my own fields. I have about 10 mu of land total.

My wheat is already in the ground — I planted it last October on 8 mu, like I always do. Wheat is the safest crop. If everything else fails, I still have wheat to eat and sell. I use Jimai 22, an improved seed that my neighbor Lao Wang has been using for years and he gets good yield. Last year I got about 1000 jin per mu, which is around 500 kg. I hope for the same this year if the weather cooperates. For the wheat, I put down compound fertilizer as base before planting, and I will topdress with urea when it starts jointing in spring. I do not weigh it exactly — I know about one bag of compound per mu and another half bag of urea later — but if you want kilograms, I guess it is about 12 kg of nitrogen per mu. I irrigate four times: once at green-up, once at jointing, once at flowering, and once at grain-filling. Water costs money now with the meters, so I watch the sky, but four times is what my family has always done. I spray twice for insects and once for weeds. I till with the rotary tiller before planting.

For cotton, I am planting 2 mu this week. Cotton prices have been decent, and my cousin does well with it. But I am 68 now — my back is not what it used to be, and cotton needs spraying every few days for bollworms. Two mu is enough. I use an improved variety, Guoxinmian. I give it compound fertilizer at planting and some urea later. I irrigate twice, maybe three times if it is very dry. The cotton will need about 15 sprays total — mostly insecticide — but that is just the way cotton is.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant maize immediately on the same 8 mu. There is no time to plough — we just plant directly into the wheat stubble. Everyone here does this double-cropping. If I only grew one crop, I would lose half my income, and my son is working in the city so I need the money. I use Denghai 605 hybrid seed. It gives good yield, about 550 kg per mu if the rains come. I put compound fertilizer in the planting hole and maybe some urea at the big trumpet stage. I irrigate twice — once at jointing and once at flowering. I spray for insects twice and for weeds once.

Why not more cotton or vegetables? Vegetables need too much labor and I am old. More cotton means more spraying than my old legs can handle. The wheat-maize double crop is my insurance — even if one crop has a bad year, the other usually saves me. I would rather use a bit more fertilizer than risk a bad yield. Losing one crop hurts more than saving a few yuan on fertilizer.
